curves.notes: Fastned's published charge curve for the Toyota bZ4X "75 kWh (2022-2025)" (read from the page's embedded chart data, one value per % SoC; every 5 % kept plus the peak). Fastned states curves show the car with the battery in optimal condition (about 30 °C) on its 300 kW-class chargers; cold or hot batteries charge slower. European market car. Fastned labels the pack 75 kWh (marketing size); the 150 kW rating and 147 kW peak match the 71.4 kWh, 150 kW FWD hardware (generation A). Starts at 9 % SoC in the source. The shape (peak about 147 kW at 25 %, 90 kW at 50 %, 39 kW at 80 %) is a 400 V NMC taper. Cars.com measured a much weaker 52 kW peak at Electrify America with a US FWD XLE (cold/unknown conditions; single test), so US winter results can be far lower. Model year not stated by Fastned; European car; spans the 2023 launch and 2024-25 charging-update generations. Contrast: Cars.com cold test of a US 2023 FWD XLE never exceeded 52 kW.

Fastned's published charge curve for the BMW i4 "83,9 kWh (2021+)" (200 kW) (read from the page's embedded chart data, one value per % SoC; every 5 % kept plus the peak). Fastned states curves show the car with the battery in optimal condition (about 30 °C) on its 300 kW-class chargers; cold or hot batteries charge slower. European market car. Peak 207.9 kW at 16 % is 4 % above the 200 kW rating (within the 5 % linter tolerance); the stepped 198.9 kW start and step drops at 17, 21, 26, 38 and 42 % are real features of the BMW curve, not smoothing. Source range 4-98 %. Same shape as the evkx.net table values seen in search excerpts (about 205 kW at 15-18 %, 107 kW near 50 %, 70 kW near 80 %), which is an independent-looking but possibly derived source and is only a sanity check. Applied to eDrive40, xDrive40, M50 (same 83.9 kWh pack, 200 kW rating in the spec batch).

Fastned's published charge curve for the Volkswagen ID.4 "77 kWh" (175 kW) (read from the page's embedded chart data, one value per % SoC; every 5 % kept plus the peak). Fastned states curves show the car with the battery in optimal condition (about 30 °C) on its 300 kW-class chargers; cold or hot batteries charge slower. European market car. Fastned shows the identical chart for the "GTX 77 kWh" (180 kW) listing, so it is one shared 77 kWh, 175-180 kW curve rather than a per-trim measurement. Peak 178.8 kW is 2.2 % above the 175 kW rating. Applied only to the 2024+ 175 kW powertrains; the 2023 Pro (170 kW rating) would exceed the 5 % ceiling by 0.3 kW so it is left out. Source range 3-89 %. Fastned lists identical data for the ID.4 77 kWh and the GTX, so the measured car is unknown; only weak second source (Cars.com ~30 min 10-80, curve integrates to 31.4 min).
